title: Did Troy Aikman Play for Oklahoma? The Hall of Famer's OU Years
question: Did Troy Aikman play college football at Oklahoma before UCLA?
answer: Yes. Troy Aikman, a Henryetta, Oklahoma, product, was a Sooner in 1984 and 1985 before transferring to UCLA. He went No. 1 overall in 1989, won three Super Bowls with Dallas and entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2006.
summary: Troy Aikman began his college career at Oklahoma in 1984-85 before UCLA, then won three Super Bowls and reached Canton in 2006. Here is how his OU stint went.
body: Ask Sooner fans to name the OU players in the Pro Football Hall of Fame and most will start with Lee Roy Selmon, enshrined in 1995, and Tommy McDonald, who followed in 1998. Troy Aikman is the great asterisk. Canton lists UCLA as his college, but his college career started in Norman.

Aikman grew up in Henryetta, Oklahoma, and was a Sooner in 1984 and 1985 under Barry Switzer. As a sophomore in 1985 he won the starting job and led OU to a 3-0 start that included a victory over Texas. On Oct. 19, 1985, against Miami, a sack by defensive tackle Jerome Brown broke his ankle and ended his season. Switzer went back to the wishbone with Jamelle Holieway, and the Sooners went on to win the national title.

Aikman wanted an offense better suited to his passing style, and Switzer helped oversee his transfer to UCLA. After sitting out 1986 under transfer rules, he started in 1987 and 1988, the Bruins won 20 games, and he collected the 1988 Davey O'Brien Award and consensus All-America honors.

The rest is NFL history. Dallas took him first overall in 1989, and over 12 seasons, all with the Cowboys, he won Super Bowls XXVII, XXVIII and XXX, earned MVP honors in Super Bowl XXVII and made six Pro Bowls. He was enshrined in Canton in 2006 and entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 2008.
So is Aikman a Sooner Hall of Famer? Officially he is a Bruin, but every OU fan who remembers 1985 knows where his story began.
